Entities recur across windows by construction (23,708 installation keys observed over 2005-2030 rows), so the row id must be the composite (registry, installation, year) and the recurring-entity property declared, not mistaken for split leakage; positives cluster weakly at the installation level (an installation's net-short status is autocorrelated year to year), so the clustered count to report is distinct installations going net-short in a window, measured at construction.

Unit: both are tonnes CO2-equivalent per installation-year (1 allowance = 1 tonne); the comparison is unit-free within the source's own frame (no external threshold or datum is involved). Frame restriction: installation-years where both VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION are numeric ('n/a' rows - not-yet-operating, excluded or closed sites - are out of frame and their handling must be pinned at construction). records.split_strategy: Temporal, one row per country-week: train ISO years <=2019, eval 2020-2022, holdout 2023 onward. Measured on the full table (country-week grain, origin streams summed, denominator >= 50): train window 2005-2019 has 14,870 usable country-weeks; eval window 2020-2022 has 8,559 usable country-weeks of which 29.0% are positives (2,485) - the COVID-era base-rate break is a property of the phenomenon and is documented, not smoothed away; holdout window 2023 has 4,677 country-weeks (42.4% positive, 1,984), extending through 2024-2026 (12,707 country-weeks, 48.3% positive, 6,135). Positives cluster by country-season: 278 clustered country-years in the eval window, 400 in 2024-2026. Construction must restrict to country-weeks where negatives are systematically reported (see measurements: pre-2015 rows are ~uniform-positive where negatives are missing, so those rows cannot carry the rate frame), and the clustered count, not the row count, is the effective sample-size figure.
records.target: Binary, computed from the source row of week W+4: influenza positivity = INF_ALL / (INF_ALL + INF_NEGATIVE) exceeds 0.10, with a minimum denominator of 50 specimens in the week. Unit: proportion of specimens testing positive for influenza. Reference frame: country x ISO week, SENTINEL and NONSENTINEL origin streams summed (the table's grain is country x ISO week x ORIGIN_SOURCE). Label source columns INF_ALL and INF_NEGATIVE are recorded in label_source_columns and must be absent from the shipped feature columns; the threshold and lead are to be pinned at construction against a named known-event fixture before any number is quoted.

At that instant the FY k audit has not been performed, so the label cannot exist. records.split_strategy: Temporal, by label year (year_end), computed from the actual audit_opinion_facts CSV (command: python3 candidates/za-municipal-audit-opinion/probe_label_stats.py <audit_opinions.csv>, scratch kept this session): train 2011-2017 = 1,863 rows / 878 positives (47.13%); eval 2018-2020 = 738 rows / 376 positives (50.95%); holdout 2021-2024 = 982 rows / 415 positives (42.26%). Both classes present in every one of the 14 label years (measured per-year rates 35.0%-56.5%). Clustered positives: audit outcomes correlate within an audit cycle/year, so the independence scale is ~14 label years, not 3,689 rows - confidence intervals must be clustered by year and the onset-conditioned variant recomputed at construction. Municipalities are repeated entities across years: features may include each municipality's own history, and the runner's id_columns handle the municipality code; no cross-split entity leakage arises because splits are by time, but the descriptor must declare expected duplicate ids.
records.target: Binary label from the audit_opinions cube ('Code' column, bulk CSV audit_opinion_facts on munimoney-media S3): 1 = qualified, disclaimer or adverse; 0 = unqualified or unqualified_emphasis_of_matter; 'outstanding' rows (audit not completed) are excluded, not imputed. Label source column is never shipped as a feature: the label CSV is used only to build y; features come from the separate incexp/cflow/capital/bsheet/grants/uifwexp/repmaint/aged-debtor/aged-creditor cubes and the demographics API. Measured per-year positive rates (qualified-or-worse, outstanding excluded): 35.0%-56.5% across all 14 label years, never degenerate. Measured persistence: 83.88% year-over-year agreement (2018-2020), so the level label is persistence-shaped and the primary task is the deterioration-onset conditioning; onset base rate measured 69/381 = 18.1% of clean-prev municipality-years in 2018-2020.
